top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a simple, general mechanism, magic-wavelength trapping, whose systematics are computed and checked. It has been reproduced at about 10^-18 in several independent laboratories and has already yielded millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and a many-body clock regime. The two-name allocation (Katori for the concept, Ye for the record regime) follows two identifiable steps, so the achievement is mature and its scope is clean. No award is the only alternative on this slate, and the lineage and tool-versus-discovery objections do not outweigh this case.
